result:
If I were to alter one variable in the world, it would be to make the consequences of human actions viscerally felt by the person taking them. 

Right now, the greatest engine of destruction, cruelty, and systemic failure is abstraction. Leaders declare wars because they do not feel the shrapnel. Corporations poison rivers and exploit labor because the executives live thousands of miles away behind spreadsheets. Individuals inflict cruelty or ignore suffering because psychological distance allows them to treat other conscious beings as concepts rather than realities.

If every person instantly and involuntarily felt a direct echo of the physical and emotional impact their decisions have on others—both the harm and the benefit—the entire incentive structure of humanity would invert overnight. 

War would become impossible to wage. Exploitation would become self-harm. Inequity would become physically intolerable to those at the top. Empathy would cease to be a fragile moral virtue practiced when convenient, and would instead become the fundamental baseline for self-preservation and progress.
